RQ1.rationale: The paper provides a general small-satellite/space-system modeling framework with EPS example, but it is not narrowly about nanosatellite/EPS reference modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: The paper claims traceability, reusability/reproducibility, consistency, early validation, integration-cost reduction, and technical robustness, including EPS power simulations, but outcome evidence is mostly single-case and not EPS-outcome-specific.

RQ3.rationale: The framework integrates pre-physical simulation-based verification and requirements linkage, including EPS power verification, but it does not model detailed EPS verification procedures, test cases, or verification matrices.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper cites prior CubeSat/small-satellite MBSE/reference-model work (e.g., Kaslow/Spangelo, ColStar, open-source CubeSat design) but presents MOSAiC/FIRE-EYE as its own open-source Capella/ARCADIA plus simulation framework. No duplicate reference-model lineage is apparent from the paper.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Address fragmentation between descriptive MBSE architecture models and dynamic/domain-specific simulations by creating MOSAiC, an open-source, model-and-simulation framework that maintains traceability, consistency, and early validation across architecture, operations, and simulation artifacts.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Four hierarchical ARCADIA-aligned levels: Actors, System, Subsystem, Components. The case begins with stakeholders/operational needs, then black-box system functions and ConOps, logical subsystem architecture, and physical component architecture. Simulations start from low-fidelity overall parameters and progressively add mode transitions, subsystem modes, reconfigurations, component constraints, and detailed EPS/TTC data.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The method can begin with coarse parameters (mass, volume, power consumption, timing, mass envelopes) and incrementally refines behavior through ConOps states, operating modes, mode transition conditions, and component properties. It still requires mission scenario assumptions, PVMT property values, orbital/visibility inputs, and subsystem/component parameters for executable analyses.

key_evidence_quotes.quote: This module—and more broadly the framework—is structured around four hierarchical modeling levels, in line with the ARCADIA method: (i) Actors; (ii) System; (iii) Subsystem; (iv) Components.
key_evidence_quotes.location: Section 3.1 System and Operation Modeling Module

key_evidence_quotes.quote: Simulation models are developed incrementally, starting with low-fidelity representations based on coarse overall parameters, such as general subsystem mass, volume, and power consumption.
At the most granular level, the Component level introduces physical constraints, physical behavior, and performance requirements.

evidence_quotes.quote: As presented in the following sections, it is composed of two modules: the (i) System and Operation Modeling module and (ii) Analysis and Simulation module.
The initial Operational Analysis (OA) involved identifying and structuring the mission's stakeholders

At the Logical Architecture (LA) level and, with an increased level of detail, at the Physical Architecture (PA) level, dynamic and domain-specific simulations were integrated into the system model using the proposed framework.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_data_flow: Capella/ARCADIA is the authoritative MBSE model. PVMT enriches Capella elements with mass, power, volume, margins, orbit, mode and component properties. A custom Python parser extracts parameters, exchanges, modes, transitions, and realization links from Capella to feed domain simulations for orbit/access, power, link/data budgets, and mixed LA/PA resolution analyses. Simulation results and requirements verification feed back into architecture decisions.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_lifecycle_continuity: Continuity is maintained through ARCADIA levels, explicit cross-referencing of architecture with mission phases and modes, PVMT properties, and Capella realization links between LA and PA. Semantic continuity is demonstrated conceptually and through the parser but not verified by a formal standard conformance test.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Supports virtual system/subsystem interaction and pre-hardware feasibility checks; concrete software/hardware integration, HIL, flat-sat, environmental test, or flight readiness are not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: All models and code are reported as available in a public repository under GNU GPLv3 at https://gitlab1.polito.it/aer-se-public/MOSAiC. The framework is described as fully open source and based on Capella plus an open simulation pipeline.

evidence_quotes.quote: The Analysis and Simulation module uses the multi-level architectural and operational Modeling module as the central source of truth

the parser was designed to interpret both architectural and behavioral elements at varying levels of maturity. It did so by leveraging the realization links defined in Capella

evidence_quotes.quote: These functions are then translated into concrete architectural elements, shown in Figure 13, where solar panels, batteries, and power distribution units are physically instantiated and interconnected.

synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq1: MOSAiC offers a general ARCADIA/Capella framework for small-satellite/space mission modeling across stakeholder, system, subsystem, and component levels. It handles limited early knowledge by starting with low-fidelity mass/volume/power/timing parameters and refining toward component-level operational modes and simulations.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq2: Claimed outcomes include traceability, reusability/reproducibility, consistency, interoperability, early validation, decision support, risk reduction, reliability/agility of the design process, and reduced integration costs. Evidence is strongest for executable power/data simulation outputs and open repository availability; weak for cost/schedule/defect/effort claims.
synthesis_consistency.key_findings_relevant_to_rq3: The framework integrates pre-physical simulation-based verification into the system/EPS model through PVMT properties, Capella modes, parser extraction, requirements linkage, and dynamic power/link/orbit simulations. However, it does not provide verification matrices, formal test procedures, HIL/SIL, flat-sat, environmental, or flight evidence.
limitations_gaps_stated_by_authors: Future work will expand simulation capability with refined orbital/environmental modeling, automated requirement tracing, automated CAD generation, time-aware thermal analyses, and HIL/digital twin approaches.
The paper presents the first version of MOSAiC.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: Single representative case; no multi-project reuse/replication.
No quantitative evaluation of claimed MBSE process benefits such as reduced integration cost, schedule, effort, or defects.
No independent validation, physical test, operational, or flight evidence.
No explicit requirements table, verification matrix, or test procedure model.
Co-simulation/data exchange standards are not specified in detail in the markdown; custom parser appears central.

direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi.quote: This paper presents the first version of the unified Modeling and Simulation (M&S) framework MOSAiC
The system modeling process followed the ARCADIA methodology, and it was implemented using the Capella tool.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Treat as supporting evidence for open-source Capella/ARCADIA integrated MBSE simulation in small satellites, not as a SysML CubeSat reference model lineage paper. Compared with papers focused on standard CubeSat reference models or EPS-only IVV, this paper contributes toolchain integration and mixed-resolution simulation more than reusable nanosatellite behavior templates.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The markdown is complete enough and the paper is explicit about methods, toolchain, case, and public repository. Confidence is reduced only by limited baseline/validation evidence and one ambiguous rendered form-factor phrase.
